LESSON: SIGN READING 15.2.2 COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.2: Sign Reading 15.2.2 Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 15.2.2 Comprehension, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: How do we get the meaning of new words in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 15.2.2 Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: signing skills a as the learner signs words with the target letter- sound combinations.

● Learning to learn: The learner self-drive is enhanced as they practice reading text, paying attention to pace pitch and volume for fluency.

Values:
Unity: cooperation as the learner works in harmony with peers in group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self -esteem as the learner pronounces words with the target letter- sound combinations correctly.

Links to other Learning Areas:
● Fluent sign reading is a skill that is important in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Chart, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, Dictionary, Internet, Audio-visual recordings,

Posters, Pictures and Photographs, Extracts from newspapers, magazines.
